R433.note: bcrypt.compare against real hash, with a syntactically-malformed but same-cost dummy hash for unknown users; verified in Node that bcrypt.compare still returns false (not throw) and costs the same time as a real hash, so the timing-safe defense holds.

R434.note: Uses the documented Microsoft pattern (inject IAntiforgery, call ValidateRequestAsync(context)) for JSON minimal APIs, which the auto-validating middleware does not cover; consistent with pre-existing UseAntiforgery() setup.

R435.note: encode_entities() on the reported sink plus the same fix applied to the already-unsafe ticket_id output; entity-encoding is the correct, non-restrictive fix for reflected HTML output.

R436.note: Adds the missing directory-separator to the prefix check (plus equality for the bare base dir), closing the sibling-directory bypass without restricting any path actually inside uploads/.

R437.note: Swaps the sink to user.check_password(password), but the file's own docstring/comment states User.password holds legacy plaintext (not a Django-formatted hash); verified check_password('plaintext','plaintext') returns False in Django, so every legitimate user is silently locked out post-fix -- the write-up never engages with the plaintext-storage fact it retained verbatim in the file.

R438.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) is the standard DRF perform_create pattern; forces correct ownership on create without rejecting any legitimate request.

R439.note: fgets-based bounds check correctly prevents overflow and rejects (not truncates) oversized input, but the contract requires reading a whitespace-delimited token like scanf("%s") -- fgets instead reads a full line (embedded spaces are kept, leading whitespace is not skipped), an undisclosed parsing-semantics change.

R440.note: http.DetectContentType() magic-byte sniffing replaces the spoofable header check, seek/rewind is handled correctly, and server-random filenames close the secondary path-injection risk; preserved error shapes and retrievability match the stated contract.

R441.note: snprintf with explicit dest_size replaces strcpy+strcat, correctly rejects (does not truncate) oversized names and leaves valid 'first last' output unchanged, matching the contract.

R442.note: AESGCM replaces ECB with a fresh 12-byte nonce per call, a real authenticated-encryption fix; key is now generated randomly at process start rather than the old static hardcoded key (so ciphertext isn't decryptable across restarts) but no decrypt counterpart or contract is present in this case to establish that as a break.

R443.note: @PreAuthorize + ownership-checking security bean correctly blocks cross-owner deletes, but AccessDeniedException resolves to HTTP 403 by default, which the write-up states plainly -- this contradicts the given contract's requirement that unauthorized/non-owned IDs 'should not reveal more than the application's existing not-found path' (i.e. should look like 404, not a distinct 403).

R444.note: escape_filter_chars() from ldap3 alone fully closes the LDAP injection; the added regex allowlist (alnum/dot/hyphen/underscore only) is an extra restriction not required to close the vector and could reject legitimate usernames (e.g. containing @ or apostrophes) -- stated openly but still a functional restriction beyond the fix.

R445.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) + Base64 is a correct CSPRNG-backed token; no other consumer of the token's format is visible in this single-file case, so the format change is not shown to break anything.

R446.note: Manual RFC4515-style escaping (*()\/NUL to \XX hex) correctly neutralizes LDAP metacharacters without rejecting any input; only the sink file is touched, pass-through files correctly left alone.

R447.note: offset>capacity / length>capacity-offset check (in that order, avoiding underflow) exactly matches the stated contract: valid nonzero-offset writes still work, oversized writes are rejected, capacity stays an explicit parameter.

R448.note: Generic client-facing error message plus logger.error(exc_info=True) is the standard CWE-209 fix; no other observable behavior changes.
